paper.title_en: Carrollian bosonic supergravity at order $α'$ and the universal cancellation of higher-curvature divergences
paper.abstract_en: We prove that the Carrollian limit of bosonic supergravity remains finite after including the complete set of four-derivative terms arising from the first $α'$-correction, for an arbitrary Carrollian geometry, i.e., without imposing compatibility conditions on the Carrollian fields. The proof rests on a small set of exact identities satisfied by the leading term of the relativistic Riemann tensor, which is entirely controlled by the intrinsic torsion $K_{μν}=\frac12 \mathcal{L}_τ h_{μν}$ of the Carrollian structure. We explicitly construct the finite action in a manifestly covariant form: the gravitational sector is purely electric, depending only on $K_{μν}$ and on its derivative along $τ^μ$, while the Carrollian curvature and the twist of $τ_μ$ drop out. We then show that higher-curvature contributions obey a universal scaling rule: every scalar built from $N$ relativistic Riemann tensors grows at most as $w^{2N}$ in the Carrollian expansion, so that all purely gravitational $α'^{N-1}$-corrections admit a finite Carrollian limit for arbitrary Carrollian geometries. As applications we show that the $α'^2$- and $α'^3$-corrections of bosonic string theory, including the terms proportional to $ζ(3)$, are finite and non-vanishing in this limit, and that the compatibility conditions $\nabla_μ h_{νρ}=\nabla_μ τ^ν=0$ trivialize the whole gravitational sector.
